📝 Summary
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added support for shared shape and property references, including edge-specific validation settings. * Prepared shape products preserve referenced definitions and function behavior after the original model is unavailable. * JSON Schema projections support referenced shape and property definitions. * Product identity now reflects changes to the retained model. * **Bug Fixes** * Recursive shape references are rejected during loading, while shared acyclic references remain supported. * Stack, preparation, and unresolved-reference failures return errors instead of partial results or conformance verdicts. * Improved error reporting across Python, command-line, C, and WebAssembly interfaces. * **Documentation** * Added guidance on recursion and resource-limit failures, with expanded Simplified Chinese translations. The PR adds model-owned shape and function catalogs, typed recursion and preparation refusals, reference-aware planning and evaluation, and model-aware product serialization. It also updates host error adapters, projection behavior, tests, and documentation. **Changes: SHACL model ownership and recursion** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Typed refusals and recursion detection**
`crates/shapes/src/error.rs`, `crates/shapes/src/shapes/parser/recursion.rs`, `crates/shapes/tests/never_panic.rs`|Adds structured recursion and preparation refusals, stack-margin processor errors, and dependency polarity. Recursive shape references are detected during parsing.| |**Model-owned definitions and references**
`crates/shapes/src/shapes.rs`, `crates/shapes/src/shapes/link.rs`, `crates/shapes/src/expression.rs`, `crates/shapes/src/shapes/parser/*`, `crates/shapes/src/schema_import.rs`|Shapes and expressions retain their model owner. Identity encoding, varint output, fixtures, allocation checks, translations, and documentation are updated.| **Priority:** ➖ Normal **Estimated code review effort:** 5 (Critical) | ~90 minutes ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant ShapesParser participant ModelOwner participant ShapePlan participant Validator ShapesParser->>ModelOwner: retain definitions and functions ModelOwner->>ShapePlan: resolve references in the active model ShapePlan->>Validator: provide fallible validation plan Validator-->>ShapePlan: return results or typed refusal ``` **Possibly related issues** - [Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf#558](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/issues/558) — Adds typed recursion refusals and host propagation, but does not implement the complete visitor contract requested by the issue. - [Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf#690](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/issues/690) — Covers regressions from the model-catalog integration, including schema import and recursive-schema behavior. - [Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf#489](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/issues/489) — Addresses SHACL recursion checks and stack-margin refusals, but not the RDFC and SPARQL UDF requirements. **Possibly related PRs** - [Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf#687](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/pull/687) — Both PRs update the SHACL admission allocation baseline.
Merge Risk: 🟡 Moderate · up to 2443e
Resolve the outstanding JSON Schema reference concerns before merging. Certain named object choices can also lose their relationship in LinkML output.
Security architecture risk: 🟡 Moderate · up to 2443e
Shared validation definitions and saved-validator compatibility change across several APIs. Inspected failure paths preserve errors rather than returning successful validation, but restored definitions receive some checks only on first use, and current-head qualification remains incomplete. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The relevant exposure is the embedding process accepting externally supplied shapes or prepared-product bytes, with effects on validation policy and reports across supported APIs. The evidence does not identify a deployed remote endpoint, tenant boundary or infrastructure privilege expansion. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — AST decoding accepts reference terms without resolving their targets. Lowering explicitly refuses unknown targets and property-reference type mismatches, and binding propagates that refusal. Successful restoration therefore does not establish full semantic reference closure, but the inspected binding path does not turn a missing target into a successful validation. - _observed_ — Common admission deliberately avoids recomputing the dataset's canonical identity. This producer-certification and consumer-digest-chain design predates the PR; it is not established here as a newly introduced weakening. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Direct and restored-product validation paths propagate preparation, binding and validation failures before report serialization. This preserves failure containment at the inspected report-producing boundaries. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Make the distinction between restored identity checks and deferred semantic reference validation explicit in the admission contract. Qualify it with a structurally valid product containing an unknown target, covering restoration, re-serialization and binding, without implying that the current behavior permits successful validation.

**Explanation** The PR description is related to the changeset. It states that SHACL parsing and preparation retain shared definition and function domains, that artifact identity hashing streams its canonical framing, and that caller-authored recursive shape catalogs produce typed refusals. These match the file summaries, which cover shapes parsing, recursion checks, error variants, identity streaming, and the shared model owner. It also names the validation scope and the open issues `#569` and `#690`, so the description is specific enough to pass.

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

body:
Review and CI repairs are pushed in 96b0ba3d3 and b049fa51c. Main was merged normally in 4397a2336 and has not advanced since. Exact hosted Rust 1.98 MSRV passed after the SCC inference correction.

All three inline review findings are addressed and their threads resolved: the rule target driver retains its fallback model, parser fixtures inspect the original catalog definitions/properties, and product restore initializes custom components and target types before rebuilding private definitions. The repeated planned-constraint lookup was also removed.

The native library run improved from 947 passes/41 failures at publication to 988 passes/one failure. The remaining logical schema round-trip repair then passed all 14 schema-import tests. This clears the original failure inventory through the full run plus the focused repair; it is not a fresh full-suite claim on the new head. Strict Shapes/CLI all-target Clippy passed before the final ordinary-import allocation adjustment, which avoids constructing an extra empty owner.

Compatibility repairs retain the bundled structural meta-schema through the existing depth/stack-bounded evaluator, keep caller-authored recursive-schema refusal, apply legacy pre-binding restrictions to reached constraints, and reconstruct emitted shared schema references. No public recursion mode or fixed-point solver is added. Inspection fixtures retain their original semantic assertions. Assembly evidence now names the actual path implementation, with the same measurement requirements; hosted confirmation remains pending.

Current-head integration/oracle checks, hosted CI and final review are still pending. Issue 569 remains open for its original solver contract. This PR's scope remains frozen; issue 690 remains open until the regressions are actually qualified.

Repairs are pushed through 2443eec1b with normal hooks and a clean worktree. The PR scope remains frozen; no new solver, format or host capability was added.

All selected local checks pass. The 989 Shapes library controls pass, and the final LinkML change additionally passes 36 focused library controls, all 139 projection cases and 29 ontology-consumer cases. All 14 previously failing integration targets now have passing targeted rechecks, including all 65 product-refusal, 41 restored-expression and 29 real CLI controls. This combines applicable full-run evidence with focused repairs; it is not a fresh whole make check execution.

Strict Shapes/CLI all-target Clippy passes with warnings denied. Full helper hygiene passes all 87 enforced jobs, 121 exact distinct groups and 150 unique prefix-free hash domains. The audited constructor-source set remains unchanged. Core's 1398 passing controls cover unchanged core inputs.

Official TypeScript 7.0.2 and GraphQL.js 16.14.0 oracles pass their exact, located-loss, list/temporal/value and reverse-import controls. The GraphQL wrong-kind acceptance was reproduced by the official oracle and fixed by removing the lone allOf wrapper; the LinkML shared object choice now preserves the class-expression carrier of its inline form. Projection pins check the complete referenced bodies and relocated losses, rather than dropping their original assertions.

All 12 allocation and seven catalog controls pass without raising original ceilings: admission is 230 allocations versus 293; cold static-root preparation is 18 allocations/3106 requested/zero additional retained/1674 peak bytes at 1/8/32 definitions. All 18 footprint, ten carried-analysis, seven ordinary product-determinism and 28 census controls pass on applicable unchanged inputs. The mutable 5608-byte fixture is supported-generator output and the frozen epoch artifact is intact.

Main was merged normally. Current-head hosted MSRV and schema-oracle checks are green; other CI and the explicitly requested stable-head independent review are still running. Merge remains blocked until those finish successfully and any findings are addressed. Initial three inline threads are fixed, replied to and resolved.

Issue 690 remains open: the full explicit recursive solver/mode requirement recorded in its item 6 belongs to the still-open issue 569 and remains outside this user-frozen PR. The bundled caller regression is repaired through its existing bounded evaluator; no LFP/GFP implementation or complete parent-issue claim is made.

@coderabbitai review

Please review the final delta through ea133b288, especially preservation of original slot carriers at shared-reference boundaries, conjunctions and annotations, and bounded expansion. Main d26bc6e64 is already merged normally. Scope remains the published shared-catalog behavior plus its review/caller regressions; the full LFP/GFP solver in #569 remains outside this user-frozen PR.

The latest repair restores the scalar/object and mixed-enum alternatives that named TypeDefinition cannot carry, and avoids the official LinkML 1.11 generator closing a named choice wrapper over an empty local attribute set. It borrows original bodies, reuses the existing slot renderer, preserves named class/ordinary scalar carriers, detects cycles/stack exhaustion and bounds anonymous expression count by source bytes. The one changed exact member pin retains both original alternatives and the existing body/cardinality assertions.

Local checks pass: 41 LinkML library tests, all 139 projection integration tests, strict Shapes all-target Clippy and the full helper/domain hygiene gate. The original Python oracle is unchanged and passes its 16 exact instance probes, 18 located losses, seven renames/reverse imports, eight list, 12 temporal and nine value-shape probes. Normal commit hooks passed; all Cargo calls, including oracle subprocesses and hooks, use the wrapper. The new head's hosted CI is still required before merge.
